paragraphs: Swamiji taught that the world we perceive through our senses is only a small piece of an infinite spiritual reality, a slice of it showing up on the level our senses can reach. How, he asked, can we make sense of that small piece without knowing what lies beyond it?

To make the point, he told a story about Socrates. One day, while teaching in Athens, the great philosopher met a Brahmin who had travelled all the way from India to Greece. Socrates told his visitor that the most important thing a human being can study is humanity itself.
The Brahmin answered at once: how can you understand man until you understand God?

Swamiji explained what the Brahmin meant. Call it God, the Infinite, the Absolute, the Unknowable, or give it no name at all. That deeper reality is the only real explanation for everything we can know, including this life we are living now. Without it, the study of man is missing its foundation.
learn: Studying people, society and the mind is valuable, but it can only go so deep without asking what lies underneath it all. Big questions about meaning are not a distraction from understanding yourself; they may be the key to it.
